title: modules/vpc-baseline: implement public/private/isolated subnet tiers + route tables; validate CIDR inputs
author: Bruno Silva
body: Context: This is the first functional cut of subnet tiering for the AWS `modules/vpc-baseline` module (alpha for Redwood Private). It adds explicit public/private/isolated subnet sets, creates/associates route tables per tier, and introduces input validation to avoid common CIDR foot-guns before we get to NAT/endpoints. What changed: (1) Subnet tier resources: `aws_subnet.public`, `aws_subnet.private`, `aws_subnet.isolated` keyed by AZ, with consistent naming + tags. (2) Route tables: a public route table with IGW default route, and separate private/isolated route tables with only local routes (NAT routing lands in PR-243). Each subnet is explicitly associated to its tier route table. (3) Variable + validation: new variables for each tier CIDR list and enable toggles; enforce: lists match AZ count when enabled, all CIDRs are distinct, and (alpha constraint) all provided subnet CIDRs must share the same prefix length across tiers to prevent inadvertent overlaps/supernetting. (We still rely on AWS to reject true overlaps, but this catches the common /23 vs /24 mistake early.) (4) Outputs: export subnet IDs by tier + route table IDs for installer integration work (ENG-4827). Notes/assumptions: isolated subnets are intended for control-plane/data-plane components that should not require direct internet egress; they are not given IGW/NAT routes here. Private subnets also do not yet have NAT routes (next PR). How to test: `terraform init && terraform apply` against the `examples/minimal` config; verify subnets land in expected AZs, public subnets have `0.0.0.0/0 -> igw-*`, private/isolated do not; validate that supplying a mismatched CIDR list length or mixed prefix lengths fails at `terraform validate`. Checklist: terraform fmt/validate passes; naming/tagging aligns with repo standards; outputs documented in README; no behavior changes outside `modules/vpc-baseline`.
commits: vpc-baseline: add subnet tier resources (public/private/isolated) keyed by AZ
vpc-baseline: create route tables and associations per subnet tier
vpc-baseline: add variable validations for CIDR list lengths + uniqueness + prefix consistency
docs: update module README with tiering inputs/outputs and topology diagram
review_conversation: Victor Alvarez (review): Route table behavior looks right for public, but can you confirm isolated subnets never get a 0.0.0.0/0 route in this PR? We should be explicit in README that NAT routing is intentionally absent until PR-243.
Bruno Silva (author): Confirmed. This PR only adds IGW route for public. Private/isolated RTs are local-only. Added a note in README under 'Alpha limitations' to make the NAT dependency explicit.

Irene Choi (review): Naming/tagging: please align Name tags to `redwood-${var.env}-${var.name}-<tier>-<az>`; also add `Tier` tag so we can query in flow logs dashboards later. (Even if flow logs land in PR-245, the tags should exist now.)
Bruno Silva (author): Updated Name tag format and added `Tier = public|private|isolated` across subnet + RT resources.

Ethan Park (review): Outputs: installer needs stable keys. Please expose `subnet_ids_by_tier` as separate outputs (`public_subnet_ids`, `private_subnet_ids`, `isolated_subnet_ids`) rather than a single map to avoid downstream jsondecode/map handling in the installer config.
Bruno Silva (author): Done. Added explicit list outputs per tier and documented them in README; left the internal locals map for DRY resource wiring.

Nina Petrova (review): CIDR overlap validation: requiring equal prefix length across tiers is a bit opinionated but acceptable for alpha. Can we improve the error message to explain the /23 vs /24 overlap case and how to fix it?
Bruno Silva (author): Improved error message in variable validation to call out mixed prefix lengths and recommend using consistent /24s per AZ for alpha.
Victor Alvarez (approval): Approved. This unblocks endpoints/NAT follow-ups and keeps the topology understandable.
Irene Choi (approval): Approved after tag/name changes.
release_notes: AWS vpc-baseline module now supports explicit public/private/isolated subnet tiers with per-tier route tables and stable outputs for downstream installer integration.
